Theme

School & learning

philosophy noun

also philosophical, philosopher, philosophise, philosophize, philosophy of life

classical

Cic. Off. 2.5: nec quicquam aliud est philosophia, sī interpretārī velīs, quam studium sapientiae (Lewis & Short)

philosophia, philosophiae f.

noun, first declension

Cicero’s own gloss: the pursuit of wisdom. The philosopher is philosophus; to philosophise, philosophārī.

Other words

  • sapientia, sapientiae f. — wisdom; philosophy

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. philosophy

    The Latin for what philosophia seeks; it can stand for philosophy itself, as in Wolff’s sapientia Sīnēnsis (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • ō vītae philosophia dux, ō virtūtis indāgātrīx expultrīxque vitiōrum!

    O philosophy, guide of life, tracker of virtue and banisher of vices!Cic. Tusc. 5.5

  • quae philosophia fuit facta philologia est

    what was philosophy has become philologySen. Ep. 108.23

See also moral, morals.

SourcesLewis & Short: philosophia · Lewis & Short: sapientia

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, s.v. philosophy.
